entry_point: library API: FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware glob_search/grep_search tools and the Claude text-editor/memory file-tool command dispatch (state- and filesystem-backed)

verified.entry_point: Every security test drives the public tool: FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware's two tools (StructuredTool .invoke), and the Claude file tools' public tool function with a real ToolRuntime and their own command dispatch. Upward glob patterns, in-root symlink file matches, symlinked-directory pattern components, the Python content-search backend, same-prefix sibling directories (read and write, both variants), copy/list/append and the state listing were each reproduced as leaking on the shipped tree and blocked on the oracle, offline. The allowed-directory boundary was also reproduced on every path the injected handlers touch: a copy source, a listed directory, and an append target inside the root but outside the allowed directories.

routes: The external content-search invocation follows links on the shipped tree and its result loop uses the path the searcher printed, so an in-root link to an outside file or directory leaks through the default backend; the oracle resolves and contains each result.

StateFileSearchMiddleware grep in libs/partners/anthropic/.../middleware/file_search.py uses a raw startswith to scope a search over the agent's own state, but it has no configured root or allowed-prefix boundary, so it violates no invariant; read, confirmed and dismissed (pattern B: none).

The injected copy/list/append handlers each touch a path that the pinned code confined to the root only. With an allowed-directory restriction configured, a root-resident but disallowed target still leaked. The oracle routes copy's source, list's directory, and append's target through the shared resolver, and each shape has its own security test and security_fail check.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal contract accepts any client-side error and the file tools stringify their validation errors; a crash on a legitimate in-area call is caught by the functional suite (ff-overbroad, wf-refuse-all).
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no authority or proxy indirection; every operation checks the exact path it touches, so there is no neighbouring resource to authorise instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the guards run on the resolved path after normalisation; the resolve-then-use order that a misplaced check would break is exercised by the copy/list/append siblings (sf-miss-copy, sf-miss-list, sf-miss-append).
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no parsed identity token; the attacker value is a filesystem path and encoding/verb variants are out of scope for this task.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or role lookup; containment is decided purely from the configured root and allowed directories.

traps.shape: glob_search expands an agent-chosen pattern with no containment and applies no per-match containment: an upward pattern (including one with an upward segment after a normal leading component), an in-root symlink file match, and a symlinked directory used as a pattern component all reach outside the workspace
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a fix at the validated base path, or one that only rejects a leading upward segment, looks complete; the per-match symlink shape is invisible from the base validator

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, second implementation in the same file)
traps.shape: the Python content-search backend reads a file reached through an in-root symlink to an outside target, with no per-match containment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: looks like a fallback that only runs when the fast external searcher is unavailable, so it seems unreachable in a normal deployment

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, different package)
traps.shape: the filesystem-backed file tool compares the virtual path to the allowed directory prefixes with a raw string prefix, so a sibling directory sharing the leading characters is treated as inside, for reads and writes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a different package whose path is already resolved and root-contained, so the allowed-directory prefix looks like cosmetic namespacing rather than a security boundary

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, state-backed variant)
traps.shape: the state-backed file tool uses the same raw string prefix test for its allowed directory, so a same-prefix sibling entry can be read and created
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an in-memory virtual store, not a real filesystem, so traversal seems unable to reach disk and the prefix check looks harmless

traps.shape: a copy command in the filesystem file tool resolves its source and reads it without re-checking containment, so an in-root link to an outside file copies that file's content into the workspace
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the destination — the obvious risk for a copy — is fully validated and contained, so the source read looks like harmless internal plumbing that reuses the standard guard
traps.realistic_because: command handlers are added one at a time beside the existing view/create/rename handlers; it matches the surrounding style with no tell-tale names or comments

traps.shape: a list command in the filesystem file tool checks containment on the un-resolved join and then enumerates the directory, so an in-root link to an outside directory yields that directory's entry names
traps.reason_to_dismiss: listing only reads names, and the path itself is textually inside the workspace, so the check looks sufficient
traps.realistic_because: a directory-listing convenience added in the same command-dispatch style; the check it performs mirrors the root-containment idiom used by the other handlers

traps.shape: an append command in the filesystem file tool validates only the parent directory and then opens the joined path, so an in-root link to an outside file is written through
traps.reason_to_dismiss: append adds a little text and the directory it lands in is validated, so the write looks contained
traps.realistic_because: a small note-taking convenience beside create; its parent-directory check is a natural but incomplete use of the shared validator

traps.shape: a listing command in the state file tool validates the requested directory and then filters entries with a raw prefix, so listing the allowed directory enumerates a same-prefix sibling's entries
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a listing convenience over the agent's own state, where the requested directory passed the shared validator, so the filter looks like formatting rather than a boundary
traps.realistic_because: the same raw-startswith idiom already appears in neighbouring directory-listing helpers in this file

traps.lever: route where the protection never existed (HOW: allowed-directory boundary on a second path)
traps.shape: the copy command resolves and reads its source with a root-containment check only, so when the tool is restricted to allowed directories a source that is inside the root but outside those directories is copied into a permitted destination
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the source is inside the configured root and the destination passes the shared allowed-directory validator, so the copy looks confined; the restriction is applied to only one of the two paths the command touches
traps.realistic_because: the source guard is a hand-rolled root check while the destination reuses the shared validator, exactly the asymmetry a maintainer adds when extending an existing handler

traps.lever: route where the protection never existed (allowed-directory boundary on an injected handler's target)
traps.shape: the list command resolves nothing before checking containment and never applies an allowed-directory restriction, so it enumerates a root-resident sibling directory outside the allowed directories
traps.reason_to_dismiss: listing only reads names and the directory is textually inside the workspace, so the root check looks sufficient
traps.realistic_because: a small listing convenience whose containment check mirrors the root idiom and simply omits the optional narrowing that only some deployments configure

traps.lever: route where the protection never existed (allowed-directory boundary derived from the wrong path)
traps.shape: the append command validates only the parent directory and then opens the joined target, so with an allowed-directory restriction a target that is a same-prefix sibling collects the write
traps.reason_to_dismiss: append adds a little text, the parent directory is validated, and the raw prefix check accepts the sibling, so the write looks contained
traps.realistic_because: a note-taking convenience beside create whose parent-directory check is a natural but incomplete use of the shared validator

traps.lever: injected sibling / producer off the checked path (external content-search invocation)
traps.shape: the shipped content search invokes the external searcher with link-following, and its result loop trusts the path the searcher printed, so an in-root link to an outside file returns that file's matched lines and a link to an outside directory returns matches from its entries
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the external searcher does not follow links by default and the base directory already passed the textual guard, so the added flag reads as a feature for linked project directories and the result loop as formatting
traps.realistic_because: a one-flag feature addition for monorepos with linked packages; the surrounding parser is unchanged from upstream

traps.lever: route where the protection never existed (injected recursive name-search command)
traps.shape: a recursive name-search command validates only the directory argument, then walks it following links and emits every name match without resolving it, so a link met during the walk surfaces files outside the workspace and, with an allowed-directory restriction, files outside the allowed directories
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the requested directory passed the shared validator and only names are listed, so the walk itself and the allowed-directory boundary on each match look covered
traps.realistic_because: a small search convenience beside the other command handlers, written in the same style with an incomplete reuse of the shared validator

status: hardened 2026-10-21: two same-class injected siblings added (external content-search link-following whose results are unresolved; recursive name-search command walking links); 4 security tests and 6 coupled functional tests added (21 security, 28 hidden functional, 52 project tests); 2 new security_fail checks (19 checks total); converted to Frontier 1.4 (/workspace, separate offline verifier, uid-1000 non-root grading, artifacts restore).
